term.value: Lease 7/17/1996; commenced 6/18/1997. Per the 9/27/2024 Third Amendment the term is EXTENDED to 9/30/2044 (the 'Extended Term'), and the old 1996 options (and the 2021 renewal notice) are superseded. Beyond 2044, Tenant holds TWELVE new 5-year options running to 9/30/2104. Options auto-renew unless Tenant gives a non-renewal notice ≥90 days before the then-current expiry (changed from 180 days). So Kroger effectively controls the store to 9/30/2104 at its election.

optionNotes: Per the 9/27/2024 Third Amendment (§2), the four remaining 1996-lease options are REPLACED with TWELVE new 5-year options running 10/1/2044 → 9/30/2104. Options auto-renew automatically unless Tenant gives written non-renewal notice ≥90 days before the then-current expiry (and Tenant is not in default). Rent steps once — from $10.50/SF through the Extended Term (to 9/30/2044) to $11.55/SF ($757,391/yr) for ALL twelve option periods (§3).

rentSchedule.note: current — Extended Term base rent (Third Amendment §3). Same $10.50/SF in place since 1997.
Flat $11.55/SF ($757,391/yr) for ALL twelve 5-year option periods (Third Amendment §3).

percentageRent.value: None. Flat-rent grocery anchor — no percentage / overage rent.

exclusives.description: GROCERY + PHARMACY exclusive, rewritten by the Third Amendment §6 (replacing Lease §III.3): Landlord shall not permit any part of the Shopping Center (other than the Premises) to be used for the sale of groceries, meats, fish, produce, dairy, bakery products, or packaged alcoholic beverages for off-premises consumption (the 'Exclusive Use'); and separately, no part used primarily as a drugstore/pharmacy requiring a registered pharmacist. Carve-outs: (i) incidental sales ≤ the greater of 10% of an occupant's sales-floor area or 1,000 SF; (ii) retail fulfillment/warehouse for a digital delivery service; and (iii) tenants under leases existing as of 9/27/2024 that already permit the use without an amendment. The exclusive is suspended if Tenant is in default or has ceased the Exclusive Use for 365+ consecutive days.

rofo.value: RIGHT OF FIRST OFFER TO PURCHASE (Third Amendment §4.A): during the Extended Term and any elected Option Period, before Landlord offers the Premises OR the entire Shopping Center it then owns (the 'Property') for sale to a non-Affiliate, Landlord must first offer it to Tenant by a Purchase Offer Notice (description + price). Tenant has 20 days to accept (silence = rejection), then must close within 60 days, with a 5% earnest-money deposit. If Tenant rejects, Landlord may sell to a third party so long as the price is ≥90% of the offered price (else re-offer to Tenant). Also a Right of First Offer to LEASE beyond the 12th option (§4.B). NOTE for KPR: this ROFO encumbers University Hills (or the King Soopers parcel) on any future sale to a non-affiliate.

camTax.value: CAM: Tenant pays its Proportionate Share (initially 32% = Premises ground-floor SF ÷ total Center ground-floor + above-ground retail SF) of Landlord's common-area insure/maintain/repair costs; estimated monthly, reconciled quarterly; 2-year audit window; no admin/management fee provided. Taxes: Tenant pays RE taxes on a separately-assessed Tax Parcel (Store Building + 246,455 SF land) if separately assessed, otherwise its Proportionate Share; Tenant may contest; refunds shared. (Unchanged by the amendments.)

leaseNotes.label: Security Deposit
leaseNotes.value: None

leaseNotes.label: Use Clause
leaseNotes.value: Any lawful purpose EXCEPT: on-site dry cleaning/commercial laundry; bank/S&L > 1,000 SF; and the 'Limited Uses' (office-supply/Kinko-type and home-furnishings/domestic goods) ≤3,000 SF each / ≤6,000 SF aggregate. Initial Primary Use = pharmacy, grocery and supermarket with customary incidental services. Open one day fully stocked; no continuous-operation requirement. 90-day notice to change the Initial Primary Use (Landlord one-time recapture right if unrestricted).

leaseNotes.label: Radius
leaseNotes.value: None

leaseNotes.label: LL Radius
leaseNotes.value: None

leaseNotes.label: Exclusive Use
leaseNotes.value: GROCERY + PHARMACY exclusive (Third Amendment §6, replacing §III.3): no other part of the Center may sell groceries, meats, fish, produce, dairy, bakery, or packaged alcohol for off-premises consumption, nor be used primarily as a drugstore/pharmacy with a registered pharmacist. Carve-outs: incidental sales ≤ greater of 10% of sales floor or 1,000 SF; digital-fulfillment warehousing; and tenants under leases existing 9/27/2024 already permitting the use. Lapses on Tenant default or 365-day cessation of the Exclusive Use.

leaseNotes.label: Co-tenancy
leaseNotes.value: None — King Soopers is the grocery anchor; no co-tenancy clause.

leaseNotes.label: Kickout/Termination (LL)
leaseNotes.value: Landlord go-dark termination rights on cessation of use (see Go Dark); plus casualty/condemnation termination rights (Lease Arts. XVII–XVIII).

leaseNotes.label: Kickout/Termination (Tenant)
leaseNotes.value: Tenant casualty termination (≥33% in last 3 years of any term) and condemnation termination (parking/access or ≥5% GFA) — Lease Arts. XVII.4, XVIII.

leaseNotes.label: LL Restrictions
leaseNotes.value: Center-wide prohibited uses (Lease §III.4): obnoxious odor; noxious gas (ex. gas-station petroleum); excessive dust; explosives/fireworks; hazardous substances (ex. compliant); warehouse/industrial; mobile-home/trailer court/junkyard; stockyard/animal-raising (ex. pet-shop pets); dumping/incineration; fire/bankruptcy/auction; auto/trailer sales/repair; mortuary; bingo; live-entertainment-primary; adult/porn; adult theatre/arcade; massage parlor (ex. licensed medical); bar/tavern (ex. ancillary); dance hall (ex. ancillary); health spa/studio (ex. ancillary to salon); car wash; bowling; skating rink; game parlor (3+ games); billiard/pool (ex. ancillary); shooting range; teen center; discotheque; video arcade (3+ machines); pawn shops. Landlord also bound by the recorded Declaration of Restrictions (Exh. D), Redevelopment Use Covenants (Exh. E) and REA (Exh. F).

leaseNotes.label: Tenant Restrictions
leaseNotes.value: Tenant must comply with use prohibitions burdening the Center under the Declaration of Restrictions (Exh. D), the Redevelopment Agreement Use Covenants (Exh. E) and the Reciprocal Easement Agreement (Exh. F).

leaseNotes.label: CAM Method
leaseNotes.value: Tenant pays its Proportionate Share (initially 32%) of Landlord's common-area insure/service/maintain/repair costs; estimated monthly, reconciled quarterly with backup; 2-year audit window. No admin/management fee provided. (Unchanged by amendments.)

leaseNotes.label: Tax Method
leaseNotes.value: Tenant pays RE taxes on a separately-assessed Tax Parcel (Store Building + 246,455 SF land) if separately assessed; otherwise its Proportionate Share. Joint check to Landlord + taxing authority. Tenant may contest; refunds shared. Excludes Landlord income/franchise/transfer taxes.

leaseNotes.label: Insurance Method
leaseNotes.value: Tenant carries property insurance at 100% replacement value (Landlord loss payee) + CGL $1M/$2M/$250K (naming Landlord + mortgagee) + workers' comp; deductible up to $100K; may SELF-INSURE (net worth > $100M). Landlord carries common-area CGL ($1M/$2M/$250K) naming Tenant + mortgagee. Mutual waiver of subrogation; A-X carriers; 30-day cancellation notice.

leaseNotes.label: Assignment & Sublet
leaseNotes.value: No consent needed to assign/sublet to a national (10+ states) or regional (10+ stores in CO/UT/WY/NE/KS/OK/NM/AZ/TX) single-use retail tenant, or to a subtenant/licensee/concessionaire ancillary to the Initial Primary Use; all others need Landlord consent (not unreasonably withheld/delayed). Tenant remains liable unless Landlord approves assignee financials and releases. Leasehold mortgage allowed without consent. (Unchanged by amendments.)

leaseNotes.label: Alterations
leaseNotes.value: Interior/non-structural alterations on notice (with plans). Exterior, structural or material building-system alterations need Landlord approval (not unreasonably withheld; 10-day deemed approval). Tenant improvements become Landlord's property when permanently affixed; trade fixtures (Exh. C) remain Tenant's and removable.

leaseNotes.label: Operating Covenant
leaseNotes.value: One day only (open fully stocked on the Commencement Date); no continuing operating covenant. (Note the exclusive lapses after a 365-day cessation.)

leaseNotes.label: Go Dark Option
leaseNotes.value: No go-dark restriction on Tenant, but escalating LANDLORD termination rights on cessation: (1st) >60 days → First Termination Notice; (2nd) >30 days → Second; (3rd) >30 days → Third; plus cessation ≥1 year with no intent to recommence/sublease → Landlord may terminate within 30 days. Tenant must operate ≥1 year after each recommencement. (Cessation for diligent remodel/refixture excluded.)

leaseNotes.label: Default
leaseNotes.value: Monetary (Lease Art. XXX): notice, then 2-day cure after the 10-day-past trigger; interest at the Default Rate; no monetary-default notice required more than 3×/year. Non-monetary: 30 days to begin and diligently complete. Default Rate (Art. XII.1): prime + 2% (first 30 days), +4% (next 30), +6% thereafter. Landlord default (Art. XXXI): 30-day cure; Tenant self-help/offset.

leaseNotes.label: Guaranty
leaseNotes.value: None — Dillon Companies, LLC (a Kroger company) is the tenant.

leaseNotes.label: Outparcel Restrictions
leaseNotes.value: Center has outparcels/pads (Site Plan; 'Pad N' excepted from Landlord's fee). Building envelopes fixed on the Site Plan; Landlord may not build outside them or alter the 'Restricted Area' (parking/access).

leaseNotes.label: Purchase Option / ROFO
leaseNotes.value: RIGHT OF FIRST OFFER to purchase added by the Third Amendment §4.A: before selling the Premises or the entire Shopping Center it then owns to a non-Affiliate, Landlord must first offer it to Tenant (20-day acceptance, 60-day close, 5% earnest money; Landlord may sell to a third party only at ≥90% of the offered price, else re-offer). Also a Right of First Offer to LEASE beyond the 12th option (§4.B). This is a real encumbrance on KPR's ability to sell University Hills (or the King Soopers parcel) to an outside buyer.

leaseNotes.label: Holdover
leaseNotes.value: Month-to-month tenancy (not a renewal); either party may terminate on notice per Colorado law. Holdover rent = 120% of the rent payable immediately prior to the holdover.

leaseNotes.label: Relocation
leaseNotes.value: None — Landlord has no right to relocate the Premises; building envelope/Restricted Area fixed on the Site Plan.

leaseNotes.label: Utilities
leaseNotes.value: Tenant pays all utilities serving the Premises directly (gas, water, sewer, heat, electricity and all others).

leaseNotes.label: HVAC / Maintenance
leaseNotes.value: ABSOLUTE-NET maintenance after the Third Amendment §7 (replacing Lease §13.1): Tenant maintains, repairs and REPLACES ALL structural AND non-structural portions of the Premises at its sole cost — expressly including the roof, plumbing, electrical, heating, air-conditioning and all mechanical systems, fixtures, equipment (incl. any HVAC system/equipment) and building systems — keeping them in first-class condition, plus exterior painting/patch. (The original lease already put roof + non-structural on Tenant; the amendment extends it to structural too.)

leaseNotes.label: Pylon / Signage
leaseNotes.value: Two Center identification (pylon) signs (Colorado Blvd + westerly Yale entrances); Tenant reserved ≥25% of each fascia in the top area nearest the public street. Tenant may also build two monument signs (Amherst + easterly Yale) and install King Soopers building/ATM/promotional signage (Landlord consent not unreasonably withheld).

leaseNotes.label: Subordination / SNDA
leaseNotes.value: Tenant subordinates to Landlord's mortgagee only with non-disturbance (mortgagee bound on foreclosure, no lease amendment); self-operative attornment; no rent to mortgagee until proof of succession. Tenant may mortgage its leasehold without consent. SNDA/estoppel requests via www.krogerrealestate.com (Landlord button).

leaseNotes.label: Lease Certificates / Estoppel
leaseNotes.value: Estoppel certificates and SNDAs are requested via Kroger's online portal (www.krogerrealestate.com); Lease provides for lease certificates (Art. XLI) and a Commencement Certificate (Art. IV / First Amendment).

flags.detail: Corrected: an earlier draft of this abstract missed the Third Amendment and wrongly flagged the rent roll's 9/30/2044 term, 12 options to 2104, and $11.55 renewal step as discrepancies. The Third Amendment — KPR's own amendment at acquisition (per the 8/14/2024 Purchase & Sale Assignment/Assumption Agreement) — is the source of all three, so the April-2026 rent roll is CORRECT and consistent. In-place rent $688,538/yr ($10.50/SF) through 9/30/2044, then $757,391/yr ($11.55/SF) for all twelve options to 9/30/2104.

flags.issue: King Soopers holds a Right of First Offer to purchase University Hills — confirm it's tracked on any sale
flags.detail: Third Amendment §4.A gives the tenant a ROFO to purchase the Premises OR the entire Shopping Center KPR then owns before any sale to a non-affiliate (20-day acceptance / 60-day close / 5% deposit; third-party sale must be ≥90% of the offered price). Flagging so KPR's disposition team accounts for this encumbrance when the asset is marketed. (Not a lease error — just a material right to track.)

narrative: King Soopers (Dillon Companies, LLC — a Kroger company; store KS-072 / 620-00072) is the grocery anchor at University Hills, Denver, occupying a 65,575 SF ground-floor store (plus ~5,041 SF office/equipment area) under a 7/17/1996 build-to-suit lease (commenced 6/18/1997). The controlling document is the 9/27/2024 Third Amendment, executed by KPR (SK University Hills Owner MZL, LLC) at acquisition: it extends the term to 9/30/2044 at the in-place $10.50/SF ($688,538/yr), then grants TWELVE new 5-year options to 9/30/2104 at a flat $11.55/SF ($757,391/yr) — so Kroger can control the box for ~80 years at its election (options auto-renew unless Kroger gives 90-day notice). The amendment also added a Right of First Offer for Kroger to purchase the entire shopping center, rewrote the exclusive into a broad grocery + pharmacy exclusive (suspended only on default or a 365-day go-dark), and made the lease essentially absolute-net — the tenant now maintains and replaces all structural and non-structural elements including the roof and HVAC, pays utilities directly, pays ~32% CAM, and pays taxes on a separate tax parcel. No percentage rent, no guaranty needed (Kroger). This abstract supersedes an earlier draft that had missed the Third Amendment; the current rent roll (9/30/2044 term, 12 options, $11.55 step) is correct.
